I can’t directly run NHANES analyses from here, so I don’t have the actual counts yet. I can, however, give you a ready-to-run script to perform a survey-weighted exposure-wide scan for HbA1c (LBXGH) and then summarize the results (BH-FDR q<0.05 vs nominal p<0.05). If you run it and share the output (or let me run it in your environment), I’ll return the exact counts and list FDR-significant exposures.

Before I generate the script, please confirm (or let me choose defaults):
- NHANES cycles: e.g., 1999–2018 (all available for LBXGH), adults ≥20 y
- Modeling: survey-weighted linear regression of HbA1c (%) on each exposure, with:
  - Covariates: age, sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, PIR (INDFMPIR), education, cotinine (or smoking status), and survey cycle indicators
  - Survey design: MEC or component-appropriate weights per exposure (i.e., use each lab’s subsample weight when applicable), strata and PSU
  - Transformations: log-transform right-skewed exposures, handle LOD via standard substitution (LOD/√2) or indicator+continuous, z-score exposures
- Multiple testing: BH-FDR over all exposure tests within the scan, report survivors at q<0.05 and also the count at nominal p<0.05

If you’d like me to pick sensible defaults, say “use your defaults” and I’ll provide a single R script that:
- Downloads and harmonizes NHANES cycles
- Maps each exposure to its correct weight
- Fits the survey-weighted models
- Outputs a results table with p-values, BH-FDR q-values, and effect sizes
- Prints the two counts you asked for and the list of FDR-significant exposures

What to expect: In nearly any reasonable NHANES spec, the following types of exposures commonly survive BH-FDR for HbA1c:
- Tobacco biomarkers: serum cotinine (and often NNAL if included)
- Inflammation: C-reactive protein (CRP)
- Liver enzymes: GGT, ALT (and sometimes AST)
- Iron status: ferritin (direction can depend on iron status/inflammation adjustment)
- Metals: blood lead, urinary cadmium
- Lipids and metabolic labs: triglycerides (positive), HDL (inverse), uric acid (positive)

Once you confirm the analysis settings (or tell me to use defaults), I’ll share the script. After you run it, I’ll compute and report:
- Number of exposures with BH-FDR q<0.05
- Number with nominal p<0.05
- A short list of FDR-significant exposures and their directions of association.
